newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RESEARCH ALERT - Argentina's Disco downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Argentina's Disco downgraded.

text.p: -- Caspian Securities announced Thursday it was downgrading Argentine supermarket chain Disco to sell from market performer due to unattractive valuation in spite of strong fundamentals.
-- Disco's 1997 price earnings of 18.7x is trading at a 35 percent premium to the local market, analysts Paula Bujia and Ricardo Cavanagh wrote in a report.

-- This premium is above other Latin American retailers' premiums respect to their markets: the Mexican average (Soriana, Gigante, Comerci and Cifra) at a 22 percent, Santa Isabel (Chile) at a 26 percent and Pao de Azucar (Brazil) at a 23 percent.
-- The stock price has gone up 81 percent since its IPO in April 1996.
-- "Although we stick to a positive view on Disco's fundamentals we believe the stock if fully-valued."
